chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, that he presented to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) the book of wergild (blood money).

And it was in it: for the loss of hearing entirely, one thousand dinars; and for the loss of voice entirely, from the sound of the nose and the hoarse sound, one thousand dinars; and the paralysis of the two hands, both of them, and the paralysis entirely, one thousand dinars; and the paralysis of the two feet, one thousand dinars; and the two lips when they are severed from the root, one thousand dinars; and the back when it humps, one thousand dinars; and the manhood when it is severed from the root, one thousand dinars; and the two testicles, one thousand dinars.
And regarding the temple of the man when he is struck, so he is not able to turn except by swerving, is half the wergild, five hundred dinars. So whatever is less than that, it is by its calculation.
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyat) for loss of hearing or paralysis in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential basis for 'diyat al-ajza' (compensation for specific body parts) by presenting a detailed tariff of injuries to Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him). It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise quantification of bodily damages, distinguishing between total loss (one thousand dinars) and partial impairment (such as the temple injury warranting half the wergild), thereby providing a practical framework for legal adjudication in cases of non-fatal trauma.
